files.cron_hour.py:
def expand_hours(field):
    base, _, step = field.partition('/')
    start, end = (0,23) if base == '*' else tuple(map(int,base.split('-')))
    return [n for n in range(start,end+1) if n % int(step or 1) == 0]
files.README.md:
# cron-hour-step

Fix expand_hours(field) to return the ascending integer hours selected by a cron hour field. Inputs are valid: "*", "*/n", "a-b", or "a-b/n", with 0 <= a <= b <= 23 and n a positive integer. Consult the document to determine how ranges, step starting points, and field boundaries affect the selected hours. No names, lists, or invalid-input validation. This is an hour-set calculation, not a scheduler.

Run: `python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests`.
Source: https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man5/crontab.5.html (DESCRIPTION: inclusive ranges and Step values (including the */23 example)).
Preserve the interface and tests. No dependencies; scratch data only in the system temporary directory.
